transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

I guess the main thing bringing me in is this almost constant restless feeling. It’s like I’m wound too tight, if that makes sense—like my body is sitting there, but inside I’m sort of buzzing or bracing or needing to move.

It shows up even in situations where I really should be calm. Like in a planning meeting at work, I’ll be trying to sit and listen, and I can do it, but it feels like I’m holding myself down somehow. Or even when I’m doing things that are supposed to be relaxing—painting, or yoga, which I actually want to enjoy—I still don’t fully settle. I keep feeling like I need to shift or do something, and it’s frustrating because I’m not trying to be difficult or impatient. It’s just this internal restlessness that doesn’t really turn off.
Along with this restless feeling, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things—like work, health, or family—even when there's no clear reason to worry?

I don’t think so, not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I worry about normal things—work deadlines, whether I forgot to answer an email, family stuff here and there—but it doesn’t feel like this big, constant mental worrying about everything, if that makes sense.

It’s more that I feel physically unsettled than mentally stuck on “what if” thoughts. Like, I’m not usually sitting there imagining terrible outcomes with my health or family or anything like that. I can get concerned when there’s an actual reason, of course, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying excessively across a bunch of areas for no clear reason. At least, that’s not how I experience it.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently—especially antipsychotics, antidepressants, or anti-nausea drugs—before this restless feeling began?

I don’t think there’s anything like that that I can clearly point to. I mean, I’d probably have to go back and look at exact dates if you needed that level of detail, because I’m not always great at remembering the timing of everything off the top of my head.

But as far as I’m aware, there wasn’t some obvious medication start or dose change right before this feeling began where I thought, “Oh, that explains it.” Nothing jumps out to me like that. If there’s something specific you want me to check, I can definitely try to verify it.

Thinking back, would you say this kind of restless, need-to-move feeling has been part of how you've felt since childhood or your teenage years, or did it start more recently as something new and different for you?

Yeah, when I really think back, it wasn’t brand-new in adulthood. I can remember it showing up pretty early, like elementary school early. I used to get notes sent home because I was always popping out of my seat, or talking over other kids, or blurting out the answer before the teacher had even finished asking the question.

At the time, I think it was treated more like I was being disruptive or not listening, and maybe sometimes I was just excited, but I do remember that feeling of not being able to just sit there quietly like everyone else seemed to. So yes, I’d say it’s been part of me since I was young, not something that just suddenly appeared recently.
